title: Changes The Board Never Hears
eyebrow: The screen follows a card being made, closed or renamed — and six other kinds of change never reach it at all

actions.fyi: You have chosen the whole screen. Nothing is waiting on you — override any decision below if you disagree with one.

content.label: What arrives and what does not
content.lead: You are right — it is partial. Half the ways a card changes never reach an open screen.

rows: A card is made, closed, renamed or moved
A note is written on a card
today yes — but only by luck, see below
A card is blocked or unblocked by another
Anything outside the cards: the project list, its counts, the side panels
Anything at all, once the connection has dropped once
only on the slow safety net, forever after

content.label: Why the missing ones are missing
content.lead: Three separate causes, not one — which is why fixing the signal did not finish the job.

items: The screen asks the board what has changed since it last looked, and a card only counts as changed if its own stamp moved. A tag edit and a blocking link do not move it. Three different readers can answer that request, and they disagree: the one serving your board ignores the question and hands back all 779 cards, which is the only reason tag and link edits reach you at all. When it is down — and it was down once already today — the screen falls back to a reader that answers the question honestly, and those edits vanish with no sign.
The screen only ever adds and corrects cards. It has no way of taking one away, so a card deleted anywhere else stays in front of you until you reload.

Only the cards were wired to the signal. The project list, its counts, the settings, the memory panel and the agents panel each load once when opened and never look again. And the listening is set up for the one project you have open, so work on any other project is silent.

blocks.label: The quiet one
blocks.text: A dropped connection is not retried. One server restart or one network hiccup and that tab stops listening for good; from then on it only catches up on the fifteen-second safety net, and nothing on screen says so.

content.label: How I know
content.lead: Measured on your own board a few minutes ago, not read off the code.

rows: yes today, because the reader ignores the request and sends everything

did not move, on either card
no — nothing ever reports a card that is gone

blocks.label: I had this wrong an hour ago
blocks.text: My first read said tag and link edits never arrive. Driving the screen's own request proved otherwise: they arrive today, because the reader answering ignores what it was asked. That is worse than it sounds — it means the board is complete by accident, and goes quietly incomplete the moment the other reader takes over.

blocks.label: Why that matters more than it sounds
blocks.text: Tags are how the board is read by system and by kind, and blocking links are what decides which work is ready. Both can change under an open screen with no sign, so the board looks current while showing you the wrong answer.

content.lead: On a copy of the whole thing — its own screen, its own board, its own cards — so nothing here was done to your board.

blocks.label: The copy is harsher than your board, on purpose
blocks.text: On the copy, tag changes never arrive. On yours they do, only because a different reader answers there. Same code, two behaviours — which is the thing worth removing, not the individual symptom.

columns: The same six, after the change
rows: The counts on the list of projects
A write after the connection was cut

blocks.label: And nothing you were doing was disturbed
blocks.text: Driven in the browser while the screen refreshed under it: an open card stayed open and on the same card, a half-typed search kept its text, and the columns neither flickered nor jumped to the top. The only movement was the new card taking its place in the order.

blocks.label: One more, found while proving it
blocks.text: A board made the ordinary way can never go live at all: the screen looks for the cards in a folder the board tool no longer writes, and quietly settles for watching a file nothing touches. On such a board not even a new card appears without a reload. Yours is not one of them; the next one somebody makes would be.

decisions.title: Every gap found is on the board as its own card, none of them patched on the way past
decisions.why: Six separate faults with three different causes. Quietly fixing whichever one was easiest to reach would leave the others invisible and the screen still partly stale.

decisions.title: A card leaving counts as a change, the same as a card arriving
decisions.why: A screen that only adds is worse than one that never updates — it looks live while holding work that no longer exists.

decisions.title: The slow safety net stays, even once every change arrives
decisions.why: It is what stands between you and a silently dead connection. It costs nothing while the signal works.

decisions.title: The whole screen goes live, not only the cards — your call, taken
decisions.why: Your words: make everything on the screen live, including the panels and the counts on the project list. So the work covers the side panels and every project's counts as well as the cards, and it is one job on the board rather than four separate fixes.

decisions.title: The screen stops asking what changed since last time and takes the board's whole answer
decisions.why: Asking for only what moved is what loses tag edits and blocking links, because those do not move a card's stamp, and it can never notice a card that is gone. Taking the whole answer fixes all three at once instead of teaching the screen three new special cases.

decisions.title: The work is done in its own copy of the screen's repository
decisions.why: Another agent is editing the same screen right now for the tags job. Separate copies mean neither of us lands on top of the other, and each change is merged on its own.

decisions.title: Correctness is bought with a bigger read each time: the whole board, 1.5 MB, in 0.027 seconds
decisions.why: Asking only for what changed is cheaper and wrong — it cannot report a card that is gone, and it drops tag and link edits whenever the honest reader answers. The whole board comes back in under three hundredths of a second against your 779 cards, which is far below anything you could see.

decisions.title: A dropped connection is retried quietly, not announced
decisions.why: The screen waits a little longer between each attempt and retries the moment you look at the window again. Nothing flashes at you, because a blip that heals itself in a second is not news; the fifteen-second safety net stays underneath either way.

next.if_nothing: I take the four pieces in order, starting with the one that makes the board quietly wrong: tags, blocking links and deletions arriving on an open screen.
